hints: Focus on what type of solution each compound makes with water, acidic or alkaline, and what that does to litmus.
Remember that most metal oxides give alkaline solutions while most metal chlorides like NaCl and CaCl2 just dissolve to give neutral solutions.
Look for the element where both its oxide and its chloride react with water to release H+ ions, so both solutions turn litmus the same way.
walkthrough:
**Recall what litmus tells us**

Think simply. Blue litmus turns red in acid, red litmus turns blue in alkali. So for both solutions to have the same effect, both must be acidic together or both alkaline together.

Rule to use:
$$\text{acidic solution turns blue litmus red, alkaline solution turns red litmus blue}$$

**Test the metals Na, Ca and Al**

Metal oxides are basic, but their chlorides (except aluminium) do not hydrolyse. That gives a mismatch.

$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH (alkaline)}$$ $$\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{neutral solution (no reaction)}$$ $$\text{CaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2 \text{ (alkaline)}$$ $$\text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{neutral solution (no reaction)}$$

**Test phosphorus, a non-metal**

Non-metal oxides are acidic, and phosphorus chlorides hydrolyse fully to give acidic solutions too. Both match.

$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 \text{ (acidic)}$$ $$\text{PCl}_5 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 5\text{HCl (both acidic)}$$

**Conclude the match**

Only phosphorus gives two acidic solutions, so both turn blue litmus red. That is the same effect on litmus.

options.A: Aluminium oxide, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, is insoluble and has no effect on litmus, while aluminium chloride hydrolyses to give an acidic solution, $\text{[Al(H}_2\text{O)}_6\text{]}^{3+} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{[Al(H}_2\text{O)}_5\text{(OH)]}^{2+} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$. The effects are different, so this is not a match.
options.B: Calcium oxide forms alkaline $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ which turns red litmus blue, but calcium chloride, $\text{CaCl}_2$, dissolves to give a neutral solution with no litmus change. Students choosing this forget that Group 2 chlorides do not hydrolyse.
options.C: Sodium oxide forms strongly alkaline $\text{NaOH}$ which turns red litmus blue, but sodium chloride, $\text{NaCl}$, gives a neutral solution. The trap is thinking both sodium compounds are alkaline, but only the oxide is.
options.D: Phosphorus is correct because both compounds give acidic solutions. Its oxide gives phosphoric acid and its chloride hydrolyses to give phosphoric acid plus hydrochloric acid, so both solutions turn blue litmus red.
